This aligns with the Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) extended to data: subtypes of the artifact set (including newly admitted evidence) must satisfy the contracts of the supertype. The supporting testing principle is contract testing over state snapshot testing.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If admission pathways can be bypassed, the universal P assertion may pass on pre-existing valid artifacts while newly admitted invalid ones are only caught if the test iterates the full set","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If P is trivially true for all artifacts (e.g., 'artifact exists'), the test provides no discriminative power","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the committed set is lazily evaluated or paginated, the test must ensure it materializes the complete set before asserting the universal quantifier","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Causal mechanism: each artifact enters the committed set through a controlled admission pathway. If that pathway enforces invariants, then any artifact passing admission necessarily satisfies P. The count is epiphenomenal \u2014 it changes as a consequence of admission events, not as a guard of correctness. Asserting P over the universal set causally verifies that the admission pathway functioned correctly for each member; asserting count==N only verifies that the net number of admission and removal events matched a fixed expectation, which has no causal bearing on individual artifact validity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
